title: gRPC & SOAP
description: Service metadata, message parsing, and authorization in RPC and SOAP interfaces.

attacks.name: gRPC reflection
attacks.desc: gRPC reflection can disclose service names, methods, and schemas when exposed to unauthorized clients.
attacks.prevention: Disable gRPC reflection on public production endpoints unless needed, or require authentication before listing methods.

attacks.name: Protobuf field fuzzing
attacks.desc: Malformed or extra protobuf fields can expose inconsistent validation between generated code and application logic.
attacks.prevention: Validate protobuf fields, types, ranges, and unknown-field policy before applying business logic.

attacks.name: gRPC auth bypass
attacks.desc: A gRPC service can lose authorization context if metadata headers are stripped or ignored between layers.
attacks.prevention: Carry trusted identity metadata across every proxy hop and authorize each gRPC method on the server.

attacks.name: gRPC-Web abuse
attacks.desc: A browser-reachable gRPC-Web endpoint may expose RPC methods that were assumed to be private.

attacks.name: SOAP action spoofing
attacks.desc: Changing SOAPAction can route a request to a different operation if it is trusted over the signed body.

attacks.name: WS-Security bypass
attacks.desc: Weak or missing WS-Security signature checks can allow SOAP messages to be modified or forged.

attacks.name: SOAP XXE
attacks.desc: Unsafe XML entity processing in SOAP bodies can expose files or trigger server-side requests.

attacks.name: WSDL exposure
attacks.desc: A public WSDL document can disclose SOAP operations, parameters, and message structure.
